issues.t: Hybrid system shuts down with "Stop Safely Now"
issues.sym: A "Stop Safely Now" message appears and the car loses drive power or shuts off while moving, sometimes after first flashing the message at startup. It may take several tries before it will start again.
issues.why: A fault in the high-voltage hybrid system makes the car protect itself by shutting down. Shops have traced cases to the DC/DC converter, the high-voltage service disconnect, the transmission control module and the electric A/C compressor, and some cars need several visits to find the cause. Owners of 2013 cars report this at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Get off the road safely, then have the car towed to a Ford dealer so the stored hybrid codes can be read before they clear. Ask the dealer to check for Ford service bulletins and software updates for your VIN.

issues.t: Power steering assist suddenly lost
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a power steering warning on the dash. It can happen while driving, which makes the car hard to turn.
issues.why: The C-Max uses an electric power steering rack. The motor or its electronics in the rack can fail, and the usual fix is a new steering gear. This is one of the most reported problems on the 2013 model, typically around 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Drive slowly and carefully to a safe place if it happens. Have the steering system codes read; if the rack has failed, it has to be replaced. Ask a dealer whether any recall or extended coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: 12-volt battery dead, car won't start
issues.sym: The car is completely dead or won't go into "Ready" mode, even though it was driven recently. It may happen repeatedly, sometimes with the clock and radio presets resetting.
issues.why: Even a hybrid relies on a small 12-volt battery to wake up its computers. On early C-Max models, modules such as the instrument cluster could stay awake and drain it, and Ford issued bulletins with software updates and part replacements. A weak original battery makes it worse.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested and replaced if weak, then ask a Ford dealer to check for software updates or bulletins for battery drain on your VIN. A jump pack can get you going in the meantime.

issues.t: Battery drained by the built-in modem
issues.sym: The 12-volt battery goes flat after the car sits, and remote phone-app features stop working.
issues.why: The telematics control unit (the built-in modem used for remote app features) can stay awake and slowly drain the battery. Ford released several service messages on this, and also warned that some non-Ford apps that access the modem can cause the same drain.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and ask a dealer to check the modem software. If you use a third-party app to talk to the car, try turning it off to see if the drain stops.

issues.t: Shifter cable bushing failure (recall)
issues.sym: The gear shown may not match the gear the car is really in, the shifter may not move the transmission into the chosen gear, or the car may roll after you select Park.
issues.why: The small bushing that connects the shift cable to the transmission can break down or fall off. Ford recalled the 2013-2018 C-Max for this.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake until the repair is done. Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the bushing and adds a protective cap for free.

issues.t: Transmission thumping or grinding noise
issues.sym: A thump, rub or grinding sound from the transmission area, often at low speed or when switching between electric and gas power.
issues.why: The HF35 hybrid transmission in cars built before mid-August 2015 can develop internal noises. Ford issued a series of bulletins with repair steps, and a later bulletin covers cleaning out contamination inside the transmission.
issues.next: Have a Ford dealer listen to it and check the noise bulletins for your build date. Catching it early may avoid a full transmission replacement.

issues.t: Door may not latch or may open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A door won't latch, keeps popping back open, or seems closed but isn't. In the worst case a door could open while you are driving.
issues.why: A part inside the side door latches can break. Ford recalled these cars to replace the latches, then recalled them again in 2020 because some earlier repairs used latches that could have the same problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls even if the doors were done before. Dealers check the latch date codes and replace them for free.

issues.t: Airbag control module may short out (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on. In a crash the front airbags, side curtain airbags and seat belt tighteners might not work.
issues.why: The protective coating on the airbag control module can crack, and humidity can then cause short circuits. Ford recalled 2013-2014 C-Max models built through November 2013.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the module replaced for free.

issues.t: Steering gear assembled incorrectly (recall)
issues.sym: Steering may feel wrong or loose, and in rare cases steering control could be lost.
issues.why: A small group of 2014 C-Max cars built in mid-August 2014 may have steering gears that were put together incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If it applies, the dealer replaces the steering gear for free.

issues.t: Car keeps running after it is switched off (recall)
issues.sym: The car stays powered on after you press the start/stop button or turn the key off, and the shifter may move out of Park.
issues.why: A body control module software problem on 2015 cars built between April 2014 and June 2015 could leave the powertrain running, which also fails theft and rollaway rules.
issues.next: Always confirm the dash goes dark before leaving the car. Check your VIN for the recall; the fix is a free software update.

issues.t: Poorly welded front floor pan (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs; the weak welds would only matter in a crash.
issues.why: Some 2016 C-Max cars had welds on the left front floor pan apron done incorrectly, which weakens the front structure.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer inspects the welds and repairs them for free.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the camera picture is fuzzy, flickers, cuts out or is blank.
issues.why: The rearview camera on some 2015-2016 C-Max models can fail. Ford opened a recall in 2025.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and back up using your mirrors until the camera is replaced for free.

issues.t: Portable charging cord can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The 120-volt charge cord that came with the car, or the outlet it is plugged into, gets very hot, smells burnt, or melts.
issues.why: Some Energi charge cords were made without a temperature sensor, so if the wall outlet has high resistance the cord can overheat and catch fire.
issues.next: Stop using the cord if it gets hot or looks melted. Check your VIN for the recall; Ford sends a replacement cord for free. Have an electrician check any outlet that got hot.

issues.t: Energi stalls or won't crank
issues.sym: The plug-in C-Max shuts down now and then, or won't start at all and shows a powertrain warning.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for 2013-2016 C-Max Energi models with intermittent stalls or no-crank conditions, plus related service messages about the high-voltage battery controller.
issues.next: Have a Ford dealer read the codes and check the stall/no-crank bulletin for your VIN. Software updates or controller repairs are the usual fixes.

issues.t: Energi won't charge or electric range drops
issues.sym: The car won't charge from a 120-volt outlet, the electric-only range changes a lot from one full charge to the next, or a check engine light comes on with charging codes.
issues.why: Ford released service messages about Energi batteries that won't charge on 120-volt chargers, electric range varying after a full charge, and charger codes P0C27/P0C28. Faults in the charging system or battery controller are the usual causes.
issues.next: Try another outlet and charger first. If it still won't charge, have a dealer read the codes; charger and battery controller problems can often be fixed with software or a single part.

issues.t: No warning chime when driver door opens (recall)
issues.sym: No chime sounds when you open the driver's door with the car still switched on.
issues.why: On some 2013 C-Max cars the reminder chime was missing, so a driver could walk away from a running car, which breaks federal theft and rollaway rules.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer fixes it for free.

issues.t: Weak A/C from electric compressor fault
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or only slightly cool, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The C-Max uses a high-voltage electric A/C compressor. Ford issued service messages for poor cooling and code P06A0 with this type of compressor.
issues.next: Have the A/C checked for refrigerant level and codes first. If the compressor is faulty, get a written estimate and ask about any Ford coverage before replacing it.

issues.t: Check engine light with camshaft codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, usually with camshaft sensor or timing codes, often without any change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Ford issued several service messages for camshaft-related codes on many 2015 and newer models, including one where moisture in the engine oil caused the codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the car drives normally it is not urgent, but book a visit and mention short-trip driving, since moisture in the oil is more common then.

issues.t: "Check fuel fill inlet" or evaporative leak light
issues.sym: A "check fuel fill inlet" message or a check engine light with evaporative system codes, sometimes coming back after repairs.
issues.why: The capless fuel filler may not seal fully, or a part of the fuel vapor system (such as a valve or the vapor canister) has a leak or fault. Ford issued a bulletin for related vapor-system codes.
issues.next: Make sure the filler flap closed fully and try refueling again. If the message stays, have the evaporative system tested; it's not urgent but can fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Real fuel economy below the original rating
issues.sym: The car averages noticeably fewer miles per gallon than the 47 mpg on the original window sticker.
issues.why: Ford lowered the 2013 C-Max Hybrid rating to 43 mpg combined after the original figure was carried over from the Fusion Hybrid under a labeling shortcut. Owners received a goodwill payment.
issues.next: Nothing needs to be fixed. Cold weather, highway speeds and short trips lower hybrid mileage further.

issues.t: MyFord Touch screen freezes or loses phone
issues.sym: The touch screen freezes, phones disconnect or contacts don't load, and radio presets or the clock reset.
issues.why: The MyFord Touch / SYNC system software has bugs, and Ford released several updates. A few cars needed module replacement.
issues.next: Do a system reset and ask a dealer or check Ford's site for the latest software update.

issues.t: Water leak stains the headliner
issues.sym: Water drips inside or leaves stains on the headliner, often after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get in through body seams or roof-area seals. Ford published a bulletin on finding and fixing water leaks that stain the headliner.
issues.next: Find the leak quickly to prevent mold and electrical damage. A dealer or body shop can water-test the car and reseal the leak.

issues.t: Leather seat cracks
issues.sym: Cracks appear on the leather seat panels or side bolsters, often on the driver's seat.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for cracking leather seat panels and bolsters on these cars.
issues.next: If the car is still under warranty, have the dealer look at it. Otherwise an upholstery shop can repair the panel.

issues.t: Front suspension rattle
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from the front over bumps.
issues.why: Worn front sway bar bushings or links are a common cause; one dealer replaced the sway bar bushings to fix it.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked, including the bushings and links.

issues.t: Wind noise from the rear windows
issues.sym: A rushing or buffeting noise at highway speed from the back windows.
issues.why: Ford noted air turbulence noise from the rear door windows at highway speeds as a characteristic of the car, with no repair recommended.
issues.next: Check that the windows are fully closed and the seals aren't damaged. Otherwise this is a normal trait.

issues.t: Car won't move from range sensor fault
issues.sym: The car powers up but won't drive, often after it has been on for a while or on a hot day, with transmission range codes.
issues.why: The transmission range sensor signal can drop out. In one documented case on a 2017 Energi, replacing the transmission, the main computer and wiring did not cure it, and the fault pointed back to the range sensor inside the transmission.
issues.next: Have it towed to a shop experienced with Ford hybrids. Ask them to check the range sensor signals and wiring before replacing large parts.
